## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

SensorReadingsSource — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/reading/SensorReadingsSource.kt

## Trigger

Opening the exercise session, via ExerciseSessionManager.registerReadingsAndStartTicker calling readingsSource.register(system.availableDataTypes()) — observed

## Today

SensorReadingsSource.register receives the set of data types
ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.availableDataTypes() reports — a call built on
ExerciseClient.getCapabilitiesAsync() (ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.kt:87) —
and, for every type in that set, calls
measureClient.registerMeasureCallback (SensorReadingsSource.kt:109).
MeasureClient's own capabilities are never read: no call to
measureClient.getCapabilitiesAsync() exists anywhere in
app-wear/src/main. SensorDataType.DISTANCE and SensorDataType.SPEED are
registered on measureClient the same way SensorDataType.HEART_RATE is
(SensorReadingsSource.kt:117-122, platformDataType mapping
DataType.DISTANCE and DataType.SPEED), even though a measure client does
not deliver those two as a punctual measurement the way it delivers
heart rate.

## Expected

SensorReadingsSource checks measureClient's own capabilities —
measureClient.getCapabilitiesAsync() — before calling
registerMeasureCallback, and registers only the data types that call
reports as supported on measureClient; ExerciseSessionManager's
availableDataTypes() (built on ExerciseClient) no longer decides what
SensorReadingsSource registers. Heart rate is read from measureClient,
as today. Distance and speed are not: they belong to the running
exercise session and must be delivered through ExerciseClient's own
session update mechanism, which nothing in app-wear reads today — no
call to an ExerciseClient exercise-update flow exists anywhere in
app-wear/src/main (a second gap: a bearer to add on the ExerciseClient
side, most likely ExerciseSessionSystem or ExerciseSessionManager,
exposing distance and speed from the session's own updates rather than
from a measure callback).
